name: Dashboard Reference: check a match and record the decision
summary: A pensions dashboard sends a possible match. A rep searches for that reference, compares what the dashboard holds against what we hold, decides whether it is the same person, and records what the decision required.

steps.title: Open the search panel
steps.action: Press Search ALPHA on the left rail.
steps.result: The panel slides out beside the rail with Search Criteria on Policy, which is what most calls start from.
steps.notes: The rail only draws the buttons this build offers and that lead somewhere. With nothing searched, Group Summary and Business Processes are not there yet.

steps.title: Choose what is being searched for
steps.action: Set Search Criteria to Dashboard Reference.
steps.result: The field below changes what it expects: the placeholder becomes a dashboard reference and the hint under it says what one looks like.
steps.notes: The criteria and the hint are the same data the call centre search reads, so the two forms cannot ask for different things.

steps.title: Enter the reference
steps.result: Search becomes pressable. A reference that does not match the shape of one is flagged on the field rather than after the search.

steps.title: Search
steps.result: The dashboard reference screen opens: the reference in the heading, the policy it resolved to, and the comparison underneath.

steps.title: Confirm what is on screen
steps.action: Read the heading and the date under it.
steps.result: Dashboard Reference: PMR12345678910, and how long that reference stays valid.
steps.notes: The reference is in the heading rather than repeated in a corner. The pension reference is not shown here because it is the policy number, which the tile below gives a line of its own.

steps.title: See the policy it resolved to
steps.result: The policy number, its status, the kind of policy it is, and how many parties are attached to it.

steps.title: Work through the comparison
steps.action: Read the differences, then open the agreements if they are needed.
steps.result: Three groups: what disagrees, what agrees, and what neither platform holds. Differences are open on arrival because they are the reason the screen exists.
steps.notes: Grouped by what the comparison found rather than field by field, so a rep is not reading forty identical rows to find the three that matter.

steps.title: Switch the layout if a table reads better
steps.action: Press Table on the layout switch.
steps.result: The same three groups, the same order, laid out as rows against columns for Dashboard Data and Our Record.

steps.title: Go to the business process
steps.action: Press Business Processes on the rail.
steps.result: On a build that shows the hub, the work plans this build offers. On a build cut to one plan, the Dashboard Reference plan opens directly.
steps.notes: The button is only on the rail once there is a plan that can be run. A plan about a dashboard reference cannot run without one.

steps.title: Open the Dashboard Reference plan
steps.result: Step one opens, headed by the reference the whole plan is about.
steps.notes: There is no hub on a build cut down to one plan, and the rail opens the plan itself. This step is the hub's.

steps.title: Say whether it is a match
steps.action: Answer 'Was this a match?' with Matched.
steps.result: A second question appears asking what the decision required. Not Matched would ask nothing further: there is nothing to record against a reference that is not this person.
steps.notes: One question at a time, and the next only once the last has an answer.

steps.title: Say what the decision required
steps.result: The categories appear. No Actions Required would end the step here.

steps.title: Record what it changed
steps.action: Tick Change of Name and Other, and write what Other was.
steps.result: The note field appears with Other, and the step has everything it needs.

do.value: Dashboard holds a second forename we do not.

steps.notes: By category rather than by field. The comparison is field by field because that is how the other platform sends it, but a given name, a surname and five alternate surnames are one change of name to everything downstream.

steps.title: Save
steps.result: The confirmation says the decision and what it required have been recorded against this dashboard reference.

steps.title: Leave the plan
steps.result: Back where the rep came from: the hub on a build that has one, and this reference's own comparison on a build that does not.
